summary: VS-031 research compendium provides comprehensive evaluation of tool and firearm content for parent-gated optional modes. Document thoroughly analyzes asset license provenance, ESRB/COPPA compliance, content rating systems, parent-gating architecture, and safe implementation patterns. Clear recommendation: REJECT realistic firearms, IMPLEMENT fantasy energy weapons and tool-based combat with comprehensive safety systems.

strengths.description: Thorough investigation of all 6 candidate assets (SWAT, Soldier, Tank, Pistol, Assault Rifle, ShooterKit) with source identification, license verification requirements, and safety assessments.
Complete ESRB rating guidelines analysis (E, E10+, T) with COPPA compliance requirements and recommendations for parent-gated content.
Clear and definitive decision: REJECT realistic firearms (Pistol.glb, Assault Rifle.glb), APPROVE fantasy energy weapons and tool-based combat with parent-gating system.
Detailed hexagonal architecture integration with ContentClassification system, ParentalControlPolicy extension, WeaponDefinition classes, and WeaponLoader with safety checks.
Comprehensive parent-gated content system design with authentication requirements, audit logging, and content type flags (energy weapons, fantasy weapons, tactical themes).
Well-designed ContentClassification enum (MELEE, TOOL, ENERGY, FIREARM, GORE) with minimum age requirements and parent approval workflows.
Numerous high-quality GDScript code samples for weapon definitions, parent policy checks, telegraph systems, and audit logging.
Comprehensive license compatibility matrix (CC0, MIT, CC-BY, GPL, etc.) with clear recommendations for each candidate asset source.
Detailed analysis of tool-based combat (hammers, wrenches, crowbars) and fantasy energy weapons (plasma, laser, ice) as safe, interesting alternatives.
Complete child-safety constraints including mandatory requirements for default safe state, explicit parent consent, reversibility, audit trail, and no exposure without approval.
Comprehensive 7-phase implementation checklist with clear testing requirements for parent controls, content access, telegraph systems, and integration.
Curated list of CC0-compatible asset sources (Kenney, Quaternius, Poly Pizza) with specific links and usage notes for safe content.

suggestions.description: Before any implementation, verify the exact source and license of each candidate asset using the provided provenance documentation templates.
Start with Phase 1 (Content Classification System) and Phase 2 (Weapon Definition System) as they provide the foundation for all parent-gated content.
Consider creating a quick-reference guide for developers on which content types are allowed by default vs. parent-gated.

notes: VS-031 provides complete evaluation of tool and firearm content for potential parent-gated optional modes.
REJECTED: Pistol.glb, Assault Rifle.glb - realistic firearms are never appropriate for Choyce Engine.
REJECTED: ShooterKit as-is - designed for realistic shooters, but technical patterns can be extracted and reimplemented safely.
APPROVED: Tool-based combat (hammers, wrenches, crowbars) - fits sandbox theme, always allowed.
APPROVED WITH PARENT GATE: Fantasy energy weapons (plasma, laser, ice) - parent-gated, E10+ rating.
APPROVED WITH MODIFICATION: Tank models - use cartoon style from CC0 sources like Kenney.
All acceptance criteria met: license provenance recorded, default sandbox stays melee-only, parent-gated with explicit policies, no asset import without approved design and safety review.
Content classification system ensures: MELEE and TOOL always allowed, ENERGY and FIREARM parent-gated, GORE never allowed.
Audit logging ensures all content access attempts are recorded with timestamps, user IDs, content IDs, and status.
The document includes 3873 lines of comprehensive research with extensive code samples, asset sources, and implementation guidance.
Integrates seamlessly with VS-005 Combat Telegraphs (wind-up system) and VS-023 Backrooms Creatures (safe monster targets).
Hexagonal architecture maintained: Domain layer (ContentClassification, ParentalControlPolicy), Application layer (weapon loading logic), Adapter layer (Godot-specific implementations).

decision.reason: Comprehensive evaluation of tool and firearm content with clear approval for safe alternatives (tools, fantasy energy weapons) and rejection of realistic firearms. All acceptance criteria met. Complete parent-gating architecture, content classification system, and safety compliance analysis provided. Ready for implementation following the 7-phase roadmap.
